label: expectations: warn, drop, fail
title: Pipeline expectations: a warn-only check still writes bad rows
definition: An expectation is a named data quality check on a pipeline streaming table, materialized view or view: CONSTRAINT name EXPECT (SQL condition). The action decides what happens to a record that fails. With no ON VIOLATION clause the action is warn: the record is written to the target and the violation is counted in the data quality metrics.
points: A11 exam-style question: EXPECT (amount >= 0) with no ON VIOLATION clause. Order 5008 arrives with -15.00. Answer: C, it is written to the table and the violation is counted. It flows on into gold totals.
ON VIOLATION DROP ROW (Python dp.expect_or_drop): the bad record is dropped before the write and the dropped count is logged.
ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE (dp.expect_or_fail): the update fails and is rolled back. Good rows are not written either, so failing the whole load over one soft problem is the other trap.
Quarantine when someone must fix bad rows: one reason per row, clean rows to silver.orders, bad rows to silver.orders_quarantine. Local run: 5 in = 2 clean + 3 quarantined.
example_note: A11 example. Expectation results are expected behavior from the Databricks docs (pipelines cannot run locally); the quarantine split was checked on local Apache Spark 4.0, not on Databricks.
misconception: An expectation is not a filter by default. Without ON VIOLATION, bad rows still land in the table.
memory_trick: Warn writes. Drop drops. Fail stops.
remember: No action means warn, and bad rows still land. DROP ROW skips them. FAIL UPDATE stops the load. Quarantine when someone needs to fix them.
